title: Endurance, splendor, foundation
hookLine: Netzach, Hod, Yesod: the lower sefirot that carry action into the world
last: TIFERET HOLDS LOVE AND STRENGTH IN HARMONY.

cards: Somewhere in the house, there's a drawer with one in it. The half-knitted scarf. The guitar with one lesson behind it.
The notebook with a few good pages and then nothing. The idea was real. The love for it was real.

Even the balance was there, for a while. What ran out was something plainer: the part that keeps walking after the excitement wears off, and the part that sets the thing down in the world where someone can use it.
Kabbalists gave those parts their own lights.

teach.h: THE ARMS, THE HEART, THE LEGS.
teach.b: Netzach, Hod, Yesod. Endurance, splendor, foundation. First, the body.
Kabbalists sometimes picture the sefirot as a human figure. Chesed and Gevurah are the arms. Tiferet is the torso, the heart.
And Netzach and Hod are the two legs. Arms reach and hold. Legs walk, carrying what was felt above into motion.
Second, the pair. Netzach, on the right, is endurance, victory, the push to keep going.

teach.h: PUSH ON, AND KNOW WHEN TO YIELD.
teach.b: Hod, on the left, is splendor, and some teachers hear in it acknowledgment, even thanks: knowing when to yield, to adjust, to say this part isn't working. Push only, and you march off a cliff.
Yield only, and you never leave the room. Third, the faces.

Some traditions link Netzach to Moses, who pressed on through the long years in the desert, and Hod to Aaron, who served in the sanctuary. Two brothers, two ways of carrying a people. Fourth, the foundation.
Below them sits Yesod, where everything above gathers before it reaches the world.
The book of Proverbs says "the righteous is an everlasting foundation," and kabbalists linked Yesod to the righteous person, and to Joseph, who kept faith in a strange land and fed the hungry.
So the lower lights aren't lesser lights. They're the ones that get the scarf finished, the meal on the table, the promise kept.

how: In Kabbalah, Netzach, Hod and Yesod are taught as the sefirot that carry the higher qualities into action; Hasidic teaching applies them to perseverance, humility and keeping one's word.

o: Netzach: pressing on, the push to keep going
putting up with pain and never complaining
a victory won once, then never needed again

games.q: the lower lights — tap the pairs.

games.q: kabbalists sometimes picture the sefirot as a body. Chesed and Gevurah are the arms. where do Netzach and Hod go?
games.why: the legs: arms reach and hold, legs walk. Netzach and Hod carry what was felt above into motion.

practice: Bring to mind one small unfinished thing, a reply you owe, a drawer half sorted, a page half read, and picture yourself doing the last step, the plain, unglamorous one.
Notice where you'd want to push on, and where you might adjust the plan so it can actually get done, and breathe into both.

wordCard.voice: Endurance. Netzach: the light of pressing on, paired with Hod, splendor, and resting on Yesod, the foundation that carries everything into the world. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: endurance, victory, lastingness. The sefirah of pressing on.

carryVoice: Your line: endure. The lower lights are the ones that finish things. See you tomorrow.
